name: Date.FormatStyle (Swift Foundation, macOS 14 / iOS 17)
verdict_reason: Apple reports a 150% improvement in one date-and-time template formatting benchmark after moving FormatStyle to Swift Foundation. No contradicting data was found; a 2026 open PR measuring a further Swift pattern formatter against ICU (1.3x-3.3x) suggests ICU is still on the path and more gains remain.
tier_reason: First-party WWDC statement about a single benchmark with no workload detail or hardware.
claimed_speedup: 'a massive 150% improvement in a benchmark of formatting with a standard date and time template'. Unmerged follow-up, ICU vs Swift pattern filling: date-format-style 1,007 ns vs 573 ns (1.76x).
workload: Format a Date with a standard date and time template.
one_liner: Apple reports a 150% speedup for Date.FormatStyle template formatting after Foundation's Swift rewrite in macOS 14 and iOS 17.
how_it_is_fast: The Swift rewrite of Foundation removed Objective-C bridging and intermediate allocations from FormatStyle. ICU still fills in the date pattern; an open swift-foundation PR moves that step into Swift as well.
use_it_when: Formatting dates for display on iOS 17+ and macOS 14+, instead of building DateFormatter instances
skip_it_when: Deployment targets below iOS 17 / macOS 14, where the old implementation runs
caveats: '150% improvement' is ambiguous (2.5x throughput or 1.5x) and covers one benchmark.
No hardware, method or code published with the WWDC claim.
The 1.76x Swift pattern formatter figure is from an open PR (October 2026) behind a build flag, not shipping code.
tradeoffs: None to adopt beyond the OS requirement.

evidence.quote: Date formatting using FormatStyle also gained some major performance upgrades, showing a massive 150% improvement in a benchmark of formatting with a standard date and time template.
